headline: Alignment-free and language-model methods for viral genome inference from reads
label: Alignment Free Viral Sequence Inference
summary: Offline nanopore pipelines and genomic language model embeddings are making viral analysis tractable without full alignment or heavy computation.
synthesis: The common thread is tractable viral sequence inference that avoids full read alignment or heavy computation. bronko performs alignment-free detection of viral SNPs, indels and minor variants directly from reads, with near-linear scaling in sequencing depth. Two embedding-based studies instead compress genomic sequence into representations: a benchmark of DNABERT-2, DNABERT-S, ViraLM and Evo2-7B against k-mer and MinHash baselines for taxonomically informative viral fragment embeddings, and MicroDUET, which adapts ProkBERT with phylogeny and function adapter heads to yield compact embeddings for scalable pathogen surveillance. EMtrace is a different modality, packaging read classification, EM-based abundance estimation and consensus assembly into an offline laptop nanopore pipeline. The new element is the shift toward lightweight, read-level or embedding-level inference, though the items differ in task and method, so this emphasis is dominant rather than shared by all.
